claims.text: The overall tribo-corrosion response of HEAs is governed by a robust in situ oxide film generated by high-temperature processing.
High-temperature processing enriches the surface in oxide-forming elements such as Al and Fe.
The resulting protective film shifts corrosion from direct metal attack to a diffusion-controlled mode.
The oxide film rapidly reforms after mechanical disruption.
Rapid film reformation reduces overall degradation relative to an alloy lacking the film.
The low-temperature baseline is a multiphase HEA without a robust continuous oxide film.
The low-temperature baseline undergoes direct-attack corrosion and has a heterogeneous surface composition.
Sintering at about 1000 °C promotes formation of a dense, continuous spinel-type oxide layer.
A continuous, dense spinel-type surface oxide is the structural mediator of the proposed response.
The oxide film slows ion diffusion and protects the underlying alloy.
The dynamic balance between mechanical film removal and oxidative film reformation governs net degradation.
The high-temperature processed HEA will have a lower corrosion current density than the low-temperature processed baseline.
The high-temperature processed HEA will exhibit a more diffusion-controlled, passivated corrosion mechanism.
Localized removal of the film may temporarily increase wear depth.
Continuous regeneration of the oxide will ultimately reduce both the wear and corrosion components of degradation.
Continuous oxide regeneration will lower total degradation relative to the low-temperature baseline.
The protective effect holds when oxygen availability and reformation kinetics are sufficient to replace film removed by wear.
The protective effect may fail under extreme wear rates or oxygen-deficient conditions.
Comparing otherwise identical high- and low-sintering-temperature specimens under identical chloride tribo-corrosion conditions tests the proposed film-mediated mechanism.

The hypothesis is falsified if the high-temperature specimen lacks a statistically significant reduction in corrosion current, lacks diffusion-controlled behavior, or has comparable or greater cumulative degradation.
